lead: Captured aviation competitor intelligence reveals active customer adoption wins across EFB and flight planning platforms, with IFS securing LCC carriers while Jeppesen and Lufthansa Systems dominate large-fleet deployments. Feed activity shows peak capture volume driven by LinkedIn and press release announcements.

insights.title: IFS Secures Multiple LCC and Regional Carrier Wins for EFBOne
insights.finding: IFS successfully captured multiple customer wins for its IFS EFBOne platform, including low-cost carrier fastjet replacing its legacy system and MY FREIGHTER (Centrum Air) adopting the software.
insights.aviation_context: fastjet is an African low-cost carrier (LCC), and MY FREIGHTER / Centrum Air is classified as an LCC with cargo operations.
insights.caveat: Captured public announcements represent visible contract wins but do not reflect the entirety of vendor market share.

insights.title: Jeppesen Secures Major Network Carriers for Flight Operations
insights.finding: Jeppesen secured significant customer deployment agreements, including Korean Air selecting Jeppesen Dispatch for its 230+ aircraft fleet and Corendon Airlines acting as launch customer for Dispatch v2026-2.
insights.aviation_context: Flight planning software integration across large widebody and narrowbody fleets requires extensive evaluation cycles.
insights.caveat: Implementation timelines and operational go-live dates are not explicitly detailed in every captured announcement.

insights.title: Competitors Release EFB and Dispatch Feature Updates
insights.finding: Multiple vendors introduced software updates, with Jeppesen launching ForeFlight FliteDeck Pro 5.3 with Enroute Profile View and Aviobook releasing AvioBook 26.3 with customizable seat swap confirmations.
insights.aviation_context: EFB feature updates typically target pilot workflow efficiency during flight preparation and execution.
insights.caveat: Feature release notices do not indicate immediate adoption rates across existing customer bases.

insights.title: Lufthansa Systems Explores Divestment of Aviation Units
insights.finding: Lufthansa Systems is reportedly exploring a sale of its Lido and NetLine business units for approximately €1bn.
insights.aviation_context: Lido and NetLine form the core flight planning, navigation, and crew management product lines for Lufthansa Systems.
insights.caveat: Reported M&A discussions in financial media are preliminary and subject to change.

insights.title: Low-Cost Carrier EFB Adoption Concentrated with IFS
insights.finding: Evidence-backed LCC customer adoptions in the captured feed are concentrated with IFS, which secured fastjet and MY FREIGHTER (Centrum Air).
insights.aviation_context: Low-cost carriers frequently seek modular EFB solutions to optimize cockpit documentation and flight-reporting workflows.
insights.caveat: LCC adoption findings are based solely on captured public signals and do not capture non-public vendor contracts.
